title: Book One · Chapter 143: The Word Our
story:
They need a name for the display. On Friday, Miss Wu gives them ten minutes. They must think about the display name.

Leo writes THE WHOLE STREET on the board. Mei looks at the small list of pictures.

“It is not the whole street.”

“It sounds larger.”

“It is still not the whole street.”

Ronan writes OUR PLACES. A girl at the front looks at his name. That could mean the school too, she says. A boy wants to call it THE BIG MAP. But there will be a game and bags too.

Miss Wu lets them talk. She lets several children give their ideas. “What does a visitor need to know?” she asks. “We have made pictures and a game. Does this name tell people that?” she asks.

Mei writes OUR RIVER STREET. The three words take up less space than Leo's first title. Ronan reads them aloud.

“Our River Street.”

“What does OUR mean here?” Leo asks. Does it mean their class? Mei says yes. It also means people living and working on River Street.

“Not every person,” Ronan says. “We asked some people. Only those people.”

They put that in the short line below the name: PICTURES, OBJECTS, AND STORIES. PEOPLE AGREED TO SHARE THEM.

Miss Wu asks them to explain the last words. Ronan says someone may let them show one thing. That does not mean they can tell every private story. He thinks of the cup in Mr Qiu's picture. He can show that. Mr Qiu's private money is different. He does not say the money part in front of the class.

They choose the name together. A few children still like THE BIG MAP better. Miss Wu writes both choices down. Each child chooses a name and raises a hand. She counts the hands. OUR RIVER STREET gets more, so that name stays.

On Saturday Ronan takes the title to Mr Qiu. The old man reads it over his glasses. Then he looks at the little drawings laid out beside it.

“Would you like to tell people about the rain?” Ronan asks.

“About the books, yes. About the payment here, no.”

Ronan writes BOOKS beside his name. Mr Qiu offers one dry pencil box for the display. It is empty and no longer needed for stock. He will lend it, not give it away.

At home Mum says yes to the bag and picture. She also agrees to a short card about the handles. The card will explain her tests. She wants the little cloth mark shown too. She chooses the words herself. Ronan copies her words slowly. Then he brings the copy back. Mum checks each line.

“You may put the green gate on the map,” Mrs Lan says. She will not lend her key. Leo wanted a real key beside each door picture. Now he draws one instead and marks it DRAWING.

Mei brings her own list on Monday. She will show two new street drawings and one page of small window studies. She will bring them inside a board cover. After the display, they must go back in that cover. Ronan copies that beside her name. Leo adds a place for covers under the table. After the visitors leave, the pictures can go back inside. Now they have a clear place to keep the covers.

That evening Dad looks over the title from his chair. He has been quiet while Ronan asks the others. Ronan brings the old-home picture to him.

“Could this come?”

Dad studies the tree and the little red bike. His thumb stops near the edge. “Let me think.”

Ronan nods. He puts the picture back between its boards. On the list beside it he writes WAIT. He reads WAIT once more. Dad has not agreed yet. Ronan must ask again, not write YES by himself.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：share them＝分享这些东西；lend＝借出；wait＝等待。

情节提示：objects＝实物；raise a hand＝举手；stock＝待售物品。

理解：1. 大家怎样选出了展示名称？2. Dad 对旧家图画的回答是什么？
